style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: 100mm macro photograph in a garage: an unbranded smartphone lies face-up on a bone-white painted-wood workbench, screen dark, a compact pocket thermal camera dongle plugged into its USB-C port, the dongle's dark germanium infrared lens and brushed steel ring in razor-sharp focus. Soft directional daylight rakes in from the left, laying a rim highlight across the lens ring and long soft falloff over the bench; graphite, bone white and ochre palette, fine dust on the painted wood, a studded drywall bay dissolving into smooth bokeh behind. Asymmetric framing, hero on the left third, generous editorial negative space to the right, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, no people, no text, no logos.
rationale: The story turns on one physical artifact and what it costs and contains — exactly the macro use case, and the article's subject is a handable product rather than a system. A 100mm close-up puts the infrared lens, the sensing core that separates the three cameras, at the razor-sharp centre of the frame while the garage workbench grounds it in the homeowner's diagnostic world. After a run of constructed, telephoto and studio treatments, a photographic macro gives the desk a fresh register.
subject: an unbranded pocket thermal camera dongle plugged into a smartphone's USB-C port, its dark germanium infrared lens in razor-sharp focus
core_thesis: The super-resolved resolution printed on the box is software; the native detector underneath is the purchase, and the $90 step from a 160×120 to a 256×192 detector is the only hardware ladder in the set — everything above it buys kit, shipping and brand, not sensing.
core_conflict: Marketed headline resolution (software upscaling, the decoy spec) versus the native detector pixel count underneath (the real sensing hardware a homeowner pays for)
composition: Asymmetric macro layout — dongle and lens on the left third, phone receding diagonally beneath it, generous editorial negative space to the right with the studded wall bay dissolving into bokeh
